title: Trap! Trap! Trap!
reviewNotes: Four branches, 18 exact positions from the supported seven-piece diagram after ...Kxb7 at 84s. Kf2 attacks Re3; illustrated d3/e4/e6/b3 retreats allow Nc5+ forks. Each king response and final rook capture is independently supplied. Resulting wins require conversion, not immediate mate. Earlier eight-piece b-pawn/Nd7 setup is context.

You see, in this position, a simple move by white like knight to C6 check is going to be enough to secure a draw for white after something like B4 and the three pawns and knight against the rook are going to be able to hold a draw. But what's the point in taking a draw when you have a pawn so far advanced? Well, some of you might say, "Well, Petro, the pawn can always be stopped by either the rook or by the king. There's no progress to be made, and we're actually just losing a pawn, and it's going to be harder to hold the draw." But you would be mistaken. You see, first of all, if the pawn here just promotes, and the rook takes, there's going to be a knight fork. And after we pick up the rook, this is actually a winning king and pawn endgame for white. But I will give you some credit. Black is not that naive and it's going to be playing king to C7 instead. Now defending the promotion and attacking the pawn. At this point, there is only one move that allows white to win. And that move is the incredible knight to D7. Knight to D7 is first of all untouchable by the king because of course if the king takes, we're simply going to promote to a queen and win the game easily. But what about the pawn? What has what has knight D7 achieved? Right, black is simply out of the woods. Or is he? There is another incredible move here. And the move is king F2, attacking the rook. And if you notice, this rook doesn't have that many squares to go to. All of the squares that I'm highlighting right now are already defended by one of the white pieces, leaving only these four squares available for the rook. If the rook goes to any one of these squares, there is always going to be a knight fork between the king and rook. Meaning that in this position, the rook is trapped and effectively black is going to lose this game after something like this, allowing white to win this incredible position.
